newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady and dull amid Japan holiday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady and dull amid Japan holiday.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were assessed steady on Monday in thin talk with the Japanese energy markets closed for a public holiday, traders said.
"Activity was expected to be slow this week, due to the public holidays and some traders are still away taking their year-end leave," a trader said.
Traders said pockets of Chinese demand were seen but none exciting enough to spur prices higher.
High sulphur 180-cst fuel oil levels was assessed Monday at $123/$125 per tonne for January loading supplies, unchanged from Friday.
The steady tone was reflected in the swaps market, where January paper was little moved from Friday at $121.25/$122.25.
Traders said most Chinese buyers have already finished buying their requirements for the 15-day long Chinese New Year holiday, starting February 7.
Traders said there were late January supplies due to arrive in Singapore from the Mideast, but they had already been placed into the bunker market.
